chunks: And it is narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, who said:

A man wrote to al-Faqīh عليه السلام concerning a man who had a mill on the river of a village, while the village belonged to one man or two men. The owner of the village wanted to channel the water to his village through other than this river on which this mill stood, and thereby disable this mill. Does he have that right or not? So he عليه السلام wrote: "He should fear Allah and act in that according to what is fair, and he should not harm his believing brother."

And regarding a man who had a canal in a village, and another man wanted to dig another canal above it, then what distance should there be between them so that one does not harm the other, in land when it is hard or soft? So he عليه السلام wrote: "According to what ensures that neither of them harms the other, if Allah the Exalted wills."

key_terms.النَّهَرِ: the river whose water use is under dispute
key_terms.الْبُعْدِ: the required distance or separation between two canals
key_terms.الْفَقِيهِ: the Imam addressed as the jurist, who provides the ruling
key_terms.الْمَعْرُوفِ: what is fair, proper, and socially recognized as right
key_terms.رَحًى: a mill dependent on flowing water for operation
key_terms.يُضَارُّ: to cause harm or injury to another party

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-ʿAskarī عليه السلام rule on water rights and preventing harm between neighboring property owners?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses water rights and property-related harm in matters of mills and canals. The ruling is grounded in taqwa, fairness, and the principle that a believer must not inflict harm upon another, with practical arrangements determined by whatever prevents damage.
